artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Enzcyclopedia - Volumes One & Two by Split Enz, released in 2025 on Chrysalis Music, is a comprehensive archival collection celebrating the 50th anniversary of the band's debut album Mental Notes (1975). This deluxe set spans five CDs or three LPs, featuring newly remastered versions of their first two albums, Mental Notes and Second Thoughts (1976), alongside rare singles, unreleased tracks, and new stereo remixes by keyboardist Eddie Rayner. The collection offers an in-depth look at the band's early progressive and art rock style, marked by theatrical arrangements and experimental sounds that laid the foundation for their later international success.

Musically, the albums showcase Split Enz's distinctive blend of rock with avant-garde and theatrical elements, reflecting their evolution from a New Zealand cult act to a band with broader appeal. The remasters and remixes highlight the intricate musicianship and creative production from their formative years, including contributions from producer Phil Manzanera. The release also includes a 40-page booklet with rare photos and commentary from band members, enhancing its value for collectors and fans. Critically, Enzcyclopedia Volumes One & Two has been praised for its meticulous curation and sound quality, providing a clearer perspective on the band's early work and serving as a strong foundation for future archival releases.
